comparability: UCR offers genuine study of ancient myth, Greek archaeology and democratic heritage, rhetoric, literary interpretation and philosophy. The strongest existing24-course programme nevertheless devotes most of its curriculum to general literary/communication methods, modern history, modern media, Renaissance art and general social research. It does not establish the defining integrated progression in Greek and Latin philology: sustained interpretation of difficult original texts using grammar/commentary, linguistic analysis of both languages, specialised epic/tragedy/lyric, post-classical Greek/Latin transmission and independent classical literary or linguistic research. World Myth & Literature explicitly includes Homer, Virgil and Byzantine romance in a global comparative frame; that substantial contribution is preserved, but it is not the specialist philological sequence. Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy provide a strong material/political case, not a substitute for the textual discipline. The second programme adds extensive modern law/EU/international politics; the stated ancient-to-modern migration question does not make those courses training in Roman evidence. Stylistics, generic adaptation and art historiography do not supply historical grammar, classical reception research or philological methods merely by adjacency. A focused reconstruction from the whole workbook retains these useful contributions but finds no further specialist classical-text progression to remedy the programme-level shortfall. No defensible complete UCR response is established. This conclusion is not based solely on missing language teaching, a degree title, a matching quota or teacher licensing.
